_doc: qBittorrent Web API preference names, see https://github.com/qbittorrent/qBittorrent/wiki/WebUI-API-(qBittorrent-5.0)#set-application-preferences. configure.py applies these and puts them back if they're changed in the UI. Keys starting with _ are notes and are skipped. Anything not listed here stays editable in the UI.
_paths: Downloads go straight to /media/torrents/<category>. There's no separate incomplete folder, so a finished torrent never moves and Radarr/Sonarr never race a rename. Keep the torrent's own folder layout; the arrs expect it.
_tmm: Automatic Torrent Management: the category picks the folder, and changing a torrent's category or a category's path moves the files.
_seeding: No global ratio or seeding-time limits. Private trackers set their own minimums (hit-and-run rules), and Radarr/Sonarr remove a torrent per indexer once its tracker's goal is met.
_queue: At most 5 downloads at once. Seeding is never queued: a queued torrent stops announcing, and the tracker counts that as not seeding.
_network: Fixed listen port, forwarded on the UniFi gateway to the qbittorrent-peers Service (192.168.1.234). UPnP and local peer discovery are off because neither works from inside a pod. DHT and PEX stay on for public torrents and magnets; qBittorrent already turns them off for private torrents. Anonymous mode stays off because trackers check the client's identity against their whitelist.
_speed: Upload is capped at 3,750,000 bytes/s (about 75% of the ISP's 40 Mbit/s uplink), so the house keeps headroom.
_disk: libtorrent 1.2 disk cache in MiB. Set explicitly because 'auto' sizes it from the node's RAM, not the pod's memory limit.
_junk: Never download executables or shortcuts, which sometimes come inside fake releases.
_webui: A login is always required, even from localhost. Host header validation lists every name the UI is reached by. Reverse-proxy mode stays off: it would make qBittorrent trust X-Forwarded-For from the Tailscale proxy, so a forged 127.0.0.1 there could pass as localhost.
